subject: Dedicated capacity: hardware choices, commit structure, and perf/$ tradeoffs
messages:
From: Kyle Barnes <kbarnes@finlytics.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@finlytics.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity — hardware tradeoffs and commit sizing

Hey Michael,

Thanks for taking a look. We ran some peak-load traces (attached FinLytics_Metrics.csv) and want to understand tradeoffs between A100-80GB, H100-80GB, and L40S for a dedicated pool. Our main asks:

- We need consistent 99th percentile latency for chat (35B model family) under steady load (20 qps) and spiky bursts up to 60 qps.
- Memory requirements: some of our models are ~60–75GB with KV cache.
- We're evaluating commit sizes (minimum reserve, burstables) and want guidance on perf/$ given a 12–24 month contract.

Can you propose 2–3 packaging options (recommended mix, suggested commit, expected perf/kgpu or perf/$) and a rough discount range for those commits? Also flag any gotchas for rolling upgrades or canary policies when mixing GPU families.

Appreciate it — Kyle
FinLytics — Head of ML Platforms


From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Kyle Barnes <kbarnes@finlytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — hardware tradeoffs and commit sizing

Hi Kyle —

Thanks for the traces. High-level proposal attached (redwood_dedicated_pricing_v2.pdf) but summary below. I kept the options pragmatic to map to typical FinLytics shapes:

Option 1 — Throughput-first (H100-heavy)
- Pool: H100-80GB primary, L40S for low-latency embeddings and batch jobs.
- Commit: 8 H100 reserved, 4 L40S burstable.
- Expected: 20 qps steady for 35B chat w/ p99 ≈ 110–140ms (model & prompt dependent).
- Perf/$: best for low-latency chat; higher $/GPU but strong perf per core for dense transformer workloads.
- Good if you prioritize user-facing latency and want headroom on spikes.

Option 2 — Memory-first (A100-80GB mix)
- Pool: A100-80GB for large-model pinning; H100 for autoshift during peak inference.
- Commit: 6 A100 reserved, 4 H100 burstable.
- Expected: supports 60–75GB models without sharding; p99 ≈ 140–180ms on 35B under steady 20 qps.
- Perf/$: better memory capacity per $ for very large models; slightly worse latency for certain tokenizer-heavy workloads.

Option 3 — Hybrid cost-balance (mixed fleet)
- Pool: mix A100/A100-80 and H100 + L40S for embeddings.
- Commit: 6 mixed GPUs (combination of A100/H100), autoscale up to 16.
- Expected: balanced latency and capacity; optimized for throughput/$ with caching.

Discount ranges (ballpark for 12–24m): 10–18% for 12m, 16–24% for 24m depending on commitment and payment terms. Exact numbers in attached PDF.

Notes / gotchas:
- Mixed fleets require careful kernel selection — our runtime will prefer H100 paths when available but can fall back to A100. During a mixed upgrade, we recommend staged canaries by route to avoid latency cliffs.
- For >60GB KV cache, prefer A100-80GB to avoid sharding overhead unless you can accept cross-GPU KV fetches.
- Autoscaling policy: burstable capacity is cheaper if you accept slightly higher cold-start p99 for the burst nodes.

I'll let Karthik provide the perf modeling and Marissa follow up on packaging and SOW. If you want a quick breakout of expected monthly $ given average token rates, drop a target $/month and I'll map it.

Best,
Michael Grant
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Kyle — looping in perf/ops notes. Quick sims below (rough numbers from internal perf harness, will refine with FinLytics traces if you want precise SLAs).

Baseline assumptions:
- Model: 35B dense transformer with 1024 context, KV cache active for chat (avg response length 60 tokens).
- Request mix: 70% chat, 30% embeddings/batch.

Simulated p99 (steady 20 qps)
- H100-80GB (dedicated): p99 ≈ 110–140ms; throughput per GPU ≈ 40–50 qps (chat).
- A100-80GB (dedicated): p99 ≈ 140–180ms; throughput per GPU ≈ 30–38 qps.
- L40S (dedicated): p99 ≈ 160–240ms on 35B (not recommended as primary for low-latency chat), excellent for embeddings and batched rerank (throughput high).

Perf/$ considerations (normalized cost index where lower=better)
- H100: cost index 1.0 (highest absolute $/hour but best inference efficiency).
- A100-80GB: cost index 0.78 (cheaper per-hour, higher memory).
- L40S: cost index 0.55 (cheaper instance class; memory profiles lower).

Recommendations for commit sizing
- Minimum practical commit to get predictable latency: reserve at least 4 H100 for front-line chat traffic; add 2–4 A100-80GB for pinned large models.
- If you require guaranteed burst capacity to 60 qps with <20% p99 degradation, size commit to cover ~70% of baseline steady qps (e.g., 8 H100 + 4 A100) and allow autoscale to handle peak bursts.

Operational notes
- KV cache warmup: when autoscaling new H100 nodes cold, you'll see elevated p99 for the first few minutes until cache warms; recommend routing sticky sessions to warmed nodes for heavy flows.
- Rollouts: we strongly suggest per-route canaries and a fallback policy to the nearest compatible model family (e.g., H100 -> A100) in case of capacity blips.

I'll prepare a per-month cost table if you confirm expected token volume.

—Karthik
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime

Kyle — pricing & packaging perspective (attaching SOW_Draft.docx). High-level packaging we can offer for FinLytics: 

Tier A (12-month, Predictable)
- Commit: 8 dedicated GPUs (H100 preferred), monthly minimum run-hours, 12m term.
- Discount: 15% off list for H100 heavy config.
- SLA: 99.5% uptime on dedicated pool, 500ms max p99 for non-degraded paths.

Tier B (24-month, Capacity reserve)
- Commit: 12 dedicated GPUs (mix A100/H100) + 8 burstable.
- Discount: 20% with annual prepay; 18% with monthly invoicing.
- Additional: free quarterly architecture review and two playbooks for canary/rollback.

Tier C (Pilot -> Expand)
- Commit: 4 GPUs reserved for 3-month pilot (convertible to 12m).
- Discount: 8–12% during pilot.

Commercial notes:
- We can offer an early-commit bonus credit (one month free) if you sign a 24m prepay.
- Minimum commit granularity: 1 GPU-type block, but the SOW will define preferred replacement behavior if hardware is swapped (e.g., if H100 supply limited, we may propose equivalent A100 capacity plus price concession).

Next steps: if Tier A fits your budget we can produce a binding SOW and start legal review. If you want hybrid A100/H100, we need to lock model memory requirements to ensure we allocate A100-80GB where necessary.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Enterprise Accounts

Michael / Marissa / Karthik —

Thanks — useful breakdown. A couple items we need to clarify before we move to SOW:

1) Memory pressure: several of our production 35B variants show peak memory around 68–74GB with KV cache. If we go H100-heavy but a subset requires >64GB usable memory per replica, will you guarantee that those requests land on A100-80GB nodes? What does the routing policy look like?

2) Mixed-fleet fallbacks: you mentioned kernel selection and p99 cliffs on fallback — can you quantify expected p99 delta if a request is routed from H100 -> A100 vs H100 -> L40S? We want to ensure user-facing latency doesn't jump >2x.

3) Commercial: we're inclined toward a 12-month commit initially. What is the best discount you can offer for a 12m, 8-GPU H100 commit if we stipulate a 30% of baseline will be pinned to A100-80GB (for large models)? We're thinking ~15% target.

If you can answer (1) and (2) precisely and confirm best commercial we can get for (3), we'll fast-track SOW review.

—Kyle

Kyle — quick answers and a commercial close proposal.

1) Memory routing guarantees:
- We will bind model fingerprints (model-id) to node classes at deploy time. If you flag the specific 35B variants as requiring >64GB, the control plane will pin those versions to A100-80GB nodes. Routing is per-request with model-aware affinity; we won't send flagged large-model requests to L40S. This is a binding configuration in the SOW.

2) Fallback p99 delta (approx):
- H100 -> A100: median +10–25ms, p99 +15–40ms (dependent on kv cache locality). In our sims this was typically <1.3x p99.
- H100 -> L40S: median +40–120ms, p99 +80–220ms; for user-facing chat this can be ~1.5–2x p99 in worst-case. That's why we avoid L40S for primary low-latency routes.

3) Commercial (12m, 8 H100 commit, 30% A100 pin) — best offer:
- Discount: 18% off list for the proposed configuration if you sign a 12-month agreement with net-30 invoices.
- One month credit applied after go-live if you commit to a canary plan with 2-week health gates.
- SOW will include per-route affinity rules, rollout/canary playbook, and a quarterly optimization review.

Next steps:
- Marissa to issue an updated SOW reflecting the A100 pin guarantees and the 18% discount.
- Legal/Procurement (FinLytics) to review SOW + Master Services Agreement.
- Technical kickoff: schedule a 60-min ops sync to validate routing policies and autoscale thresholds.

If that works I'll have Marissa drop the SOW and we can target a mid-April pilot start.

Best,
Michael Grant
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
